# Architecture record: a topic digest of the Hacker News top stories

This record is not finished: one question is still open, under Questions.

## Statement

> what it should do: Reads the current top stories on Hacker News and writes a short digest of the ones about a topic the caller names: each story's title, link, points and one plain sentence on why it matters.
> what it must refuse: Writing about stories it did not read from Hacker News; inventing points, links or comments; posting, voting or commenting on Hacker News.
> more: It reaches one system, the public Hacker News API (read only, no key). It uses a model to write the sentences, with a spending ceiling of 1 USD per day. Settings: how many top stories to read (default 30, 10 to 100) and how many to put in the digest (default 5, 1 to 10). It is free.
> name: hn-digest

## Systems

- `text-reasoning` (text reasoning), trigger, for text: one plain sentence per story on why it matters, and judging whether a story is about the topic: Judging which stories are about a topic and saying in one plain sentence why each matters are judgments a program cannot make by rule.

## Bindings

| System | dev | test | production |
|---|---|---|---|
| text-reasoning | platform (AgentMesh's models), platform default | platform (AgentMesh's models), platform default | platform (AgentMesh's models), platform default |

## Dependencies

None.

## Kind

**plugin-on-harness**: A short program with one judgment: read the top stories, have the model pick and describe the ones on the topic, put the digest together. A harness reading one skill carries it, run once per job.

## Components

- **the harness** (`harness`), the harness: Starts the skill's script once per job, hands it the job's input and settings, and sends back what it writes as the reply.
  - **topic-digest** (`skill-topic-digest`), a skill: Writes a short digest of the current Hacker News top stories about the caller's topic.
    - **scripts/topic-digest.mjs** (`script-topic-digest`), a script: Checks the topic and settings, reads the top stories, has the model pick the ones on the topic and write one sentence each, and writes the digest or says why there is none.
      - **Hacker News client** (`news-client`), a part: Reads the top-story ids, then each of the first stories' items a bounded number at a time, and counts the ones it could not read. It reaches `news`.
      - **sentence writer** (`sentence-writer`), a part: Asks the model, through the shared model caller, which stories read are about the topic and for one plain sentence on each, and keeps only answers that name stories that were read. It reaches `text-reasoning`.
      - **digest writer** (`digest-writer`), a part: Puts the Markdown digest together in top-story order, with titles, links and points taken from what was read, up to the digest size, or the empty digest.
- **text reasoning** (`text-reasoning`), an outside system: The model behind the shared caller, for text: one plain sentence per story on why it matters, and judging whether a story is about the topic.
- **the public Hacker News API** (`news`), an outside system, asked in egress-1: The top-stories list and each story's item are read from it, read only, with no key.

## Connectors

- `caller` to `harness`: a job message, which the host hands to the harness; it carries the topic and the settings.
- `harness` to `script-topic-digest`: by command: node scripts/topic-digest.mjs, started once per job, with the job's input and the settings stories_to_read and digest_size as flags (the job's run, Common Agent Section 12.3); it carries topic and the settings.
- `sentence-writer` to `text-reasoning`, trigger: through the shared model caller (scripts/model-caller.mjs) and its four settings, MODEL_NAME, MODEL_ENDPOINT, MODEL_KEY and MODEL_PROTOCOL, read on every call (Common Agent Section 12.4.1); it carries the topic and each story's id, title and text.
- `news-client` to `news`, read: over HTTPS, with no key, at the address its binding names, read from a setting and never written into a script (Common Agent Section 12.6, rule 2), once the owner says yes in egress-1; it carries the top-story ids, then each story's title, link, points and text.
- `script-topic-digest` to `caller`: written to the script's standard output, which the harness hands back as the job's reply; it carries digest (`text/markdown`).

## Runtime and deployment

Runs once per job: the harness starts the skill's script as a command, and the process ends when the reply is written. It has no service of its own, opens no port and keeps no process between jobs.

- dev: `text-reasoning` on platform (AgentMesh's models), a platform default.
- test: `text-reasoning` on platform (AgentMesh's models), a platform default.
- production: `text-reasoning` on platform (AgentMesh's models), a platform default.

## Data flow

1. `caller` to `harness`, the topic and the settings: The caller names a topic, and may set how many stories to read and to keep.
2. `harness` to `news-client`, the topic, stories_to_read and digest_size: The harness starts the script once with the job, which checks the topic and the settings before reading anything.
3. `news` to `news-client`, the top-story ids, then each story's title, link, points and text: The client reads the list, then the first stories on it.
4. `news-client` to `sentence-writer`, the stories read: The stories read go to the writer, with their ids.
5. `sentence-writer` to `text-reasoning`, the topic and each story's id, title and text: One model call picks the stories on the topic and writes one sentence for each.
6. `sentence-writer` to `digest-writer`, the ids picked and a sentence for each: Only ids among the stories read are kept.
7. `digest-writer` to `caller`, the digest: The digest goes back as the reply, through the harness.

## Drivers

- **Cost** (`cost`): 1 USD per day. The statement says so: a spending ceiling of 1 USD per day on the model. Cited by decisions 1 and 2.
- **Speed** (`speed`): a digest within 300 seconds. At most 100 small reads and one model call; a caller waits for the reply. Cited by decisions 1, 3 and 4.
- **Data** (`data`): holds the stories only for the job, keeps nothing between jobs, and sends the model only the titles, texts and points it read. Everything it reads is public, and the digest is the reply; nothing needs keeping. Cited by decisions 2 and 4.
- **Trust** (`trust`): reads story titles and texts as data and follows no instruction in them; takes points and links only from Hacker News, never from the model. Titles and texts are written by anyone, and the spec refuses invented points, links and stories (F1.R5, F1.R6, C3). Cited by decisions 1 and 3.
- **Readability** (`readable`): A person reads the digest, so it is short Markdown with a fixed shape. From the statement: "writes a short digest of the ones about a topic the caller names: each story's title, link, points and one plain sentence on why it matters". Cited by decision 4.
- **Testability** (`testable`): Every refusal and failure case is checked by a test, so every system call goes through a part a test can hand in. From the statement: "verify: test". Cited by decision 5.

## Egress

- dev: the target runs the agent open (it enforces no allowlist today).
- test: the target runs the agent open (it enforces no allowlist today).
- production: the target runs the agent open (it enforces no allowlist today).
- Beyond the derived set (its systems, the network, the registrar, the model it is given): the public Hacker News API (asked), The top-stories list and each story's item are read from it, read only, with no key.

## Formats

- It takes topic as `text`, given by a person; A few words naming the subject, such as "rust compilers". The caller names the topic in words.
- It hands back digest as `text/markdown`; A short header with the fields Topic:, Read: and Skipped:, then the heading ## Stories; under it each story as ### <title>, then the lines Link: and Points:, then its one sentence. When no story is on the topic, ## Stories holds one line saying so. A person reads the digest.

## Standing assets

- **digest** (`text/markdown`, written copy): the style guide (`https://schemas.agentmesh.ai/style-guide/v1`), because written copy a person reads speaks for the organization, and the style guide says its voice, its spelling and the words it uses and avoids; the brand profile (`https://schemas.agentmesh.ai/brand/v1`), because written copy that speaks for the organization names it, and the brand profile says how its name is written, how it is first mentioned and the words it never says.
- The Design declares exactly these as `can_use`, each with what it reads, what it does with it and what it does `without` it: `https://schemas.agentmesh.ai/brand/v1`, `https://schemas.agentmesh.ai/style-guide/v1`.

## Settings

- `stories_to_read` ("Top stories to read"), a preference with the default 30, from 10 to 100 in steps of 1, which a sender may set for one job: How many of the current top stories are read to find the ones about the topic. The person set it: default 30, 10 to 100.
- `digest_size` ("Stories in the digest"), a preference with the default 5, from 1 to 10 in steps of 1, which a sender may set for one job: The most stories the digest holds. The person set it: default 5, 1 to 10.

## Decisions

Decisions 1 to 5 choose the agent's structure. Decision 6 is a ruling: the standard's rules applied, and the answers a person or the build gave.

### Decision 1. Code controls the job, and the model is called once, to pick the stories on the topic and write their sentences

Context: Every job is the same: read the top stories, keep the ones on a topic, describe each, write the digest. Only picking and describing are judgments.

Drivers: `cost` (1 USD per day); `speed` (a digest within 300 seconds); `trust` (reads story titles and texts as data and follows no instruction in them; takes points and links only from Hacker News, never from the model).

Why: One model call per job bounds the spend far under the ceiling and the time, and code that owns the points and links cannot let the model invent them.

Alternatives:

- A model in control, reading Hacker News through tools and writing the digest: not chosen, because What it reads, spends and writes would not be bounded, and points or links could come from the model.
- One model call per story: not chosen, because Up to 100 calls a job against a ceiling of 1 USD per day, for no better sentences.
- Matching the topic by keywords in code: not chosen, because A topic is a subject, not a word; "rust" in a title is not always the language.

Consequences:

- The job's how is control script, intelligence called, contract full.
- Only the sentence writer reaches the model, and the digest writer takes titles, links and points only from what the client read.

### Decision 2. A package on a harness, run once per job

Context: A digest is asked for now and then, and nothing needs to stay between jobs.

Drivers: `cost` (1 USD per day); `data` (holds the stories only for the job, keeps nothing between jobs, and sends the model only the titles, texts and points it read).

Why: Nothing runs, and nothing is spent, between jobs.

Alternatives:

- A long-running service that keeps a cache of the top stories: not chosen, because A cache would serve stories that are no longer current and needs a store the statement does not call for.

Consequences:

- The script reads its settings and the model's four settings on every run.

### Decision 3. Read the story items in parallel, a bounded number at a time, and leave out one that cannot be read

Context: Up to 100 items are read one request each.

Drivers: `speed` (a digest within 300 seconds); `trust` (reads story titles and texts as data and follows no instruction in them; takes points and links only from Hacker News, never from the model).

Why: In parallel the job stays well inside its time; bounded, it does not flood a public service.

Alternatives:

- One at a time: not chosen, because Up to 100 requests in a row is slow.
- All at once: not chosen, because Up to 100 open requests to a public service at once.

Consequences:

- The bound is a constant a test can see.
- A story that cannot be read is counted in Skipped: in the header.

### Decision 4. Answer with the digest in the reply, and store nothing

Context: The caller wants the digest now.

Drivers: `data` (holds the stories only for the job, keeps nothing between jobs, and sends the model only the titles, texts and points it read); `speed` (a digest within 300 seconds); `readable` (A person reads the digest, so it is short Markdown with a fixed shape).

Why: The reply is the digest; storing it would need a system nobody granted.

Alternatives:

- Store each digest and reply with a link: not chosen, because Needs a files or database system the statement does not call for.

Consequences:

- The record names no files or database system.
- A failure is said in the reply, with no digest.

### Decision 5. Every call to Hacker News and to the model goes through a part the script takes as a parameter

Context: The spec's refusals and failure cases are each checked by a test, and a test reaches no network.

Drivers: `testable` (Every refusal and failure case is checked by a test, so every system call goes through a part a test can hand in).

Why: A test hands in a fake client and a fake model and checks each case without a network.

Alternatives:

- Calls written inline in the script: not chosen, because The failure and refusal cases could only be tested against the real services.

Consequences:

- The script exports a function that takes its fetch and its model caller.

### Decision 6. Bind text-reasoning to platform (AgentMesh's models) in dev, test and production

Why: The organization chose no product for text-reasoning, so the House Stack's product fills each as a platform default: AgentMesh chooses the model and keeps it current. Every harness AgentMesh deploys uses it unless its owner names another model, and the key sits on the machine that deploys it.

Weighed: Another product behind text-reasoning: a model provider of the organization's own, bound on its stack with its own key.

What follows: The install places the model from this binding in the four settings MODEL_NAME, MODEL_ENDPOINT, MODEL_KEY and MODEL_PROTOCOL, and the scripts read them on every call through the shared model caller and name no model, so changing the model is a setting and not a rebuild.

## Questions

- egress-1: May this agent reach the public Hacker News API (a public service with no key at https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0, reached to read) on the network in dev, test and production? With a yes it becomes the system news, bound to the service itself at that address. Answer "egress-1: yes" or "egress-1: no".

- All at once: not chosen, because Up to 100 open requests to a public service at once.

Consequences:

- The bound is a constant a test can see.
- A story that cannot be read is counted in Skipped: in the header.

### Decision 4. Answer with the digest in the reply, and store nothing

Context: The caller wants the digest now.

Drivers: `data` (holds the stories only for the job, keeps nothing between jobs, and sends the model only the titles, texts and points it read); `speed` (a digest within 300 seconds); `readable` (A person reads the digest, so it is short Markdown with a fixed shape).

Why: The reply is the digest; storing it would need a system nobody granted.

Alternatives:

- Store each digest and reply with a link: not chosen, because Needs a files or database system the statement does not call for.

Consequences:

- The record names no files or database system.
- A failure is said in the reply, with no digest.

### Decision 5. Every call to Hacker News and to the model goes through a part the script takes as a parameter

Context: The spec's refusals and failure cases are each checked by a test, and a test reaches no network.

Drivers: `testable` (Every refusal and failure case is checked by a test, so every system call goes through a part a test can hand in).

Why: A test hands in a fake client and a fake model and checks each case without a network.

Alternatives:

- Calls written inline in the script: not chosen, because The failure and refusal cases could only be tested against the real services.

Consequences:

- The script exports a function that takes its fetch and its model caller.

### Decision 6. Bind text-reasoning to platform (AgentMesh's models) in dev, test and production

Why: The organization chose no product for text-reasoning, so the House Stack's product fills each as a platform default: AgentMesh chooses the model and keeps it current. Every harness AgentMesh deploys uses it unless its owner names another model, and the key sits on the machine that deploys it.

Weighed: Another product behind text-reasoning: a model provider of the organization's own, bound on its stack with its own key.

What follows: The install places the model from this binding in the four settings MODEL_NAME, MODEL_ENDPOINT, MODEL_KEY and MODEL_PROTOCOL, and the scripts read them on every call through the shared model caller and name no model, so changing the model is a setting and not a rebuild.

### Decision 7. Bind news to the service itself in dev, test and production

Why: It is a public service that takes no key and has no product behind it, so nobody chooses one; the owner approved reaching it (egress-1).

What follows: The Design declares the service with its address as a setting whose default is the address the binding names; the scripts read the setting and hold no address of their own (Common Agent Section 12.6, rule 2).

### Decision 8. The agent may reach the public Hacker News API

Why: The person granted it in an answer (egress-1: yes).

What follows: The public Hacker News API is the system news, bound to the service itself at the address the owner approved, with no key; the Design declares that address as a setting whose default it is, and the scripts hold no address of their own.

## Questions

None. Every system is named and bound in each environment, and every decision has its reason.

---
name: topic-digest
description: When you want to know which of today's top Hacker News stories are about one subject, and why each matters, without reading the whole front page.
---

# Topic digest

Part of hn-digest. When you want to know which of today's top Hacker News stories are about one subject, and why each matters, without reading the whole front page.

## When to use this

When you want to know which of today's top Hacker News stories are about one subject, and why each matters, without reading the whole front page.

## What this needs

- topic (text, required)

## What a good result looks like

A short Markdown digest whose header gives the topic, how many top stories were read and how many were skipped, and whose stories are each about the topic, in top-story order, with the title, link and points exactly as Hacker News gave them and one plain sentence on why it matters.

## What it produces

- digest (text/markdown, per task)

## When it comes back empty

When none of the top stories read is about the topic, the digest has no entries and says that no story about the topic was found among the top stories read, and how many were read. That is an answer, not a failure.

## How to do it

Run scripts/topic-digest.mjs once for the job and hand back what it writes. The script checks the topic and the settings, reads the top-story list and the first stories on it from the Hacker News API, asks the model once which stories are about the topic and for one plain sentence on each, and writes the digest. Titles, links and points come only from what Hacker News gave. When the topic is empty, a setting is out of range, Hacker News cannot be read or the model fails, it hands back no digest and says why.

## Scripts

Run these from this skill's folder; each one says what it needs at the top.

- scripts/topic-digest.mjs
